Fortress creature-list training/status source grammar

This file records grammar reconstructed from actual Ghidra 12.1.4 C output
and the original configured PE instruction/jump-table bytes. It is source
material, not a test, display check, acceptance report, or runtime observation.
The TSV productions are native output rules; they are not generated runtime
translations or sample inputs.

SOURCES

reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000:
  creature-list-status-renderer: 0x1425c40..0x1427be4; code ends 0x1427acc.
  creature-identity-training-short: 0x1330880..0x1330c2c.
  creature-identity-training-full: 0x1330c30..0x13312b8.
  creature-activity-status: 0x138f620..0x138ffc4.
  creature-activity-status-color: 0x138ffd0..0x1390cf0.
classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000:
  creature-list-status-renderer: 0x1420bb0..0x1422b54; code ends 0x1422a3c.
  creature-identity-training-short: 0x132b7f0..0x132bb9c.
  creature-identity-training-full: 0x132bba0..0x132c228.
  creature-activity-status: 0x138a590..0x138af34.
  creature-activity-status-color: 0x138af40..0x138bc60.

Read the corresponding reference-*.c and classic-*.c files for actual C,
native-switches.tsv for every native selector alias, native-branches.tsv for
the original branch instructions, and native-images.tsv for paths and hashes.
The C switch overrides use those original native table targets; they do not
invent additional text choices. Both editions contain the grammar below.
Offsets below are byte offsets from the native unit object, not Ghidra's
inferred pointer-array indexes. Function names describe this source inventory.

TRAINING COLUMN

F = U32(unit + 0x110)
T = U32(unit + 0x138)
C = (F & 0x02000000) != 0                 # bit 25: caged
H = (F & 0x08000000) != 0                 # bit 27: chained
R = (F & 0x04000000) != 0                 # bit 26: training-state branch

When the renderer selects its training path:
  label = "Tame"                        if !R
  label = "Semi-Wild"                   if R and (T == 0 or T > 7)
  label = "Trained"                     if R and T == 1
  label = "Well-trained"                if R and T == 2
  label = "Skillfully trained"          if R and T == 3
  label = "Expertly trained"            if R and T == 4
  label = "Exceptionally trained"       if R and T == 5
  label = "Masterfully trained"          if R and T == 6
  label = "Domesticated"                if R and T == 7

The comparison is unsigned. Values outside 0..7, including the bit pattern of
a negative signed value, use Semi-Wild. The register bound is r11d=7, set at
reference 0x1425dbd / classic 0x1420d2d. Native dispatch is reference
0x1427564 / classic 0x14224d4; table is 0x1427bc4 / 0x1422b34.

  suffix = " (Caged)"                   if C
  suffix = " (Chained)"                 if !C and H
  suffix = ""                           if !C and !H
  training_status = label + suffix

Caged wins when both flags are set; this writer never emits both suffixes.
All nine label paths converge before the same suffix selection and the final
text submission. training-productions.tsv lists the resulting 27 rules once,
with source RVAs for both editions. The leading ASCII space in either suffix
and the original capitalization/hyphenation are part of the native text.

The native display colors are separate from the text: Semi-Wild selects 6,
training levels 1..6 select 7, and Tame/Domesticated select 2; all set the final
bright flag to 1. Translation does not need to reinterpret these colors.

SELECTION OF ACTIVITY INSTEAD OF TRAINING

The renderer first handles the death/missing branch, then calls the existing
predicate reference 0x138ed20 / classic 0x1389c90. A true result admits the
training/activity group. Within this group, the color activity formatter takes
precedence when all of the following source conditions hold:
  QWORD(unit + 0xd80) == 0;
  (U32(unit + 0x82c) & 0x02000000) == 0;
  and either
    I32(unit + 0x1280) > 7 and (BYTE(QWORD(unit + 0x1278) + 7) & 4) != 0,
    or U32(unit + 0x828) has bit 25 set.
Otherwise this group reaches the nine-label training grammar above.

The color formatter is called at reference 0x14275cb / classic 0x142253b,
with the current unit and the same text destination/color fields. Existing
non-text predicates are recorded as call boundaries; no guessed creature
category name is substituted for their actual source conditions.

OTHER STATUS BRANCHES IN THE SAME RENDERER

The bit-1 branch of F uses historical-figure existence/death flags and the
native membership/civilization conditions to choose "Missing" or "Deceased".
These are literal strings assembled with optimized fixed-width loads. The
substring loads "ing", "g", "ent", "t", and "b" in native-literals.tsv
are pieces of complete strings, not additional display productions.

If the native training/activity predicate is false and the game-mode global
is not 4, the relationship helper reference 0x138ef40 / classic 0x1389eb0
supplies the following unsigned selector. Native relationship dispatch is
reference 0x142711b / classic 0x142208b. S is the same mutually exclusive
empty/Caged/Chained suffix grammar defined above.

  0, 11       "Wild Animal" + S
  1           ("Undead" if QWORD(unit+0xd80) != 0 or
               (U32(unit+0x118) & 0x1000) != 0; else "Opposed to life") + S
  2, 3, 4, 7  "Caged Prisoner" if C; else "Chained Prisoner" if H;
               else "Hostile"
  5, 14       "Berserk" + S
  6           "Invader" + S
  8           diplomat lookup succeeds: "Diplomat / " + activity_plain + S;
               else merchant lookup succeeds: "Merchant" + S;
               else I32(unit+0x118) < 0: "Guest / " + activity_plain + S;
               else "Visitor" if U32(unit+0x114) has 0x800000 set,
                    otherwise "Friendly"; then append S
  9           "Underworld" + S
  10          if reference 0x138ee20 / classic 0x1389d90 is false:
                 "Caged Prisoner" if C, else "Chained Prisoner" if H,
                 else "Hostile";
               otherwise the Guest/Visitor/Friendly branch described for 8
  12          "Caged Guest" if C; else "Chained Guest" if H;
               else "Uninvited Guest"
  13          "Current Resident" + S
  15          "Undead" + S
  16          "Agitated Caged Creature" if C;
               else "Agitated Chained Creature" if H;
               else "Agitated Wilderness Creature"
  >16         same Prisoner/Hostile branch as 2, 3, 4, 7

The embedded Caged/Chained Guest/Prisoner/Agitated branches submit their text
directly; they do not pass through the extra suffix writer. By contrast,
Diplomat and Guest prefixes wrap the actual plain activity output and then
append S. Do not flatten a supplier's existing suffix and the renderer's
outer suffix into one invented grammar step.

When this predicate is false and game mode == 4, I32(unit+0x1270) == 0 gives
"Independent"; other values give "#" + the native formatted numeric value.
Its 15-way modulo switch selects colors only and does not add other words.
"Job" is the column heading in the same renderer, not a status value.

ACTIVITY FORMATTERS

Both complete activity functions are retained as source, including early
returns and dynamic supplier boundaries. Their text families are:
  job formatter result (current job object with its 0x10000 flag);
  active activity/order virtual formatter result;
  active activity virtual formatter result, optionally followed by "!";
  "Return Treasure";
  "Conduct Meeting";
  "Attend Parley";
  "Attend Meeting";
  "Make Request of " + native site-name formatter;
  native item formatter + " at " + native site-name formatter;
  "New Arrival";
  "No activity";
  "Mercenary", "Monster Slayer", or "Soldier";
  "Noble";
  "No job";
  the child/baby no-occupation branch: empty text, "Caged", or "Chained".

The native job/item/site/activity formatter results remain typed supplier
nonterminals. They are not a new finite list inferred from spelling, and
custom names are not normalized by this source grammar.

For the soldier-family branch an existing order object appends one of these
failure suffixes, selected by its virtual status result:
  0   " (not following order)"
  1   " (activity cancelled)"
  2   " (no barracks)"
  3   " (improper barracks)"
  4   " (no activity)"
  5   " (cannot individually drill)"
  6   " (does not exist)"
  7   " (no archery target)"
  8   " (improper building)"
  9   " (unreachable location)"
  10  " (invalid location)"
  11  " (no reachable valid target)"
  12  " (no burrow)"
  13  " (not in squad)"
  14  " (no patrol route)"
  15  " (no reachable point on route)"
  16  " (invalid order)"
  17  " (no temple)"
  18  " (no library)"
  19  " (no item)"
  20  " (cannot leave site)"
  21  " (location no longer in zone)"
  unsigned values >= 22: " (cannot follow order)"
No order object means no failure suffix.

The profession gate before these choices uses (I16(unit+0xa0) - 75) <= 22,
with an unsigned comparison. All 23 values 75..97 map to the same body:
  reference plain table 0x138ff50, remap 0x138ff54;
  reference color table 0x1390c7c -> 0x139086a, remap 0x1390c80;
  classic plain table 0x138aec0, remap 0x138aec4;
  classic color table 0x138bbec -> 0x138b7da, remap 0x138bbf0.
The 23 original remap bytes are all 00. Consequently Ghidra's "Switch with
1 destination removed" warning describes collapse of a one-target switch;
the native-switches.tsv keeps each original selector alias. No source text
branch is hidden behind that warning.

There is a real distinction at the final fallback restraint writer:
  activity_plain appends " (Caged)" or " (Chained)" to its fallback result.
  activity_color assigns " (Caged)" or " (Chained)" to its fallback result
    (reference call at 0x1390c24; classic at 0x138bb94), replacing that result.
  The child/baby branch separately assigns bare "Caged" or "Chained".
Thus a complete display value can be the leading-space suffix itself.
Early returns from job, active-activity, meeting, request and item/site paths
precede this final fallback restraint writer; do not automatically append S
to every activity supplier output.

IDENTITY-ROW TRAINING MARKERS

Both identity formatters append the following only when F bit 26 is set:
  identity_training_suffix = " (" + marker(T) + ")"
  T=0     marker = "Semi-Wild"
  T=1     marker = "Trained"
  T=2     marker = "-Trained-"
  T=3     marker = "+Trained+"
  T=4     marker = "*Trained*"
  T=5     marker = BYTE(0xf0) + "Trained" + BYTE(0xf0)
  T=6     marker = BYTE(0x0f) + "Trained" + BYTE(0x0f)
  T=7     marker = "Tame"
  unsigned T>7: marker = "Semi-Wild"

0xf0 and 0x0f are original single-byte CP437 game glyph codes, not UTF-8
sequences or ASCII punctuation. The C signed-char assignment -0x10 is the
same byte 0xf0. Preserve this distinction from the expanded status-column
labels "Exceptionally trained", "Masterfully trained", and "Domesticated".
Without F bit 26 these identity functions append no training parentheses.
The original gender marker bytes 0x0b/0x0c and optional 0x78 decoration are
separate identity-format choices preceding training; they are not labels in
the status column. Existing name/species/profession suppliers remain intact.
